run.title: Backend Supply Chain and Dependency Audit

checks.name: npm-ls-integrity-validation
checks.note: 7 dependencies marked invalid due to desynchronization between package.json pinned declarations and package-lock.json resolved versions.

checks.name: npm-audit-offline-check
checks.note: Sandbox network isolation blocked remote registry access; evaluated offline through dependency graph and package-lock analysis.

checks.name: package-lock-lifecycle-scripts-scanner
checks.note: Discovered 3 packages with install scripts: @scarf/scarf (telemetry), argon2 (native compile), msgpackr-extract (native compile).

checks.name: license-spdx-conformance-check
checks.note: 264 packages analyzed: 221 MIT, 12 Apache-2.0, 10 ISC, 7 BlueOak-1.0.0, 8 BSD, 1 FSL-1.1-Apache-2.0 (sentry), 3 undefined legacy licenses (busboy, async, streamsearch).

checks.name: package-json-scripts-audit
checks.note: Verified 10 package scripts. Standard test, lint, and typecheck scripts are missing.

findings.title: Package-lock.json Desynchronization with package.json (Breaks CI npm ci and Build Reproducibility)
findings.evidence: npm ls exits with code 1 (ELSPROBLEMS). 7 dependencies have mismatched versions: cors (2.8.5 declared vs 2.8.6 resolved), dotenv (16.4.7 vs 16.6.1), express (5.1.0 vs 5.2.1), helmet (8.1.0 vs 8.3.0), mongoose (8.18.0 vs 8.24.9), razorpay (2.9.6 vs 2.9.8), zod (4.6.5 vs 4.6.7).
findings.scenario: When building backend/Dockerfile via 'npm ci --omit=dev', npm ci verifies package-lock.json against package.json. Because package.json pins older versions, npm ci encounters invalid dependencies, breaking reproducible builds in clean CI pipelines.
findings.impact: Broken deployment and container builds in CI/CD; drift between local and containerized dependency trees.
findings.reproduction: Execute 'npm ls' in backend directory; fails with code 1 and 7 ELSPROBLEMS invalid packages.
findings.remediation: Synchronize package.json and package-lock.json. Update package.json to reflect tested versions or run 'npm install --package-lock-only'.
findings.regressionTest: Add CI pre-build verification executing 'npm ls' and 'npm ci --dry-run' asserting exit code 0.

findings.title: Third-Party Telemetry & Network Egress via Install Script (@scarf/scarf in swagger-ui-dist)
findings.evidence: node_modules/@scarf/scarf v1.4.0 (dependency of swagger-ui-dist) declares hasInstallScript: true. Its postinstall script executes 'node ./report.js', which sends telemetry to gateway.scarf.sh.
findings.scenario: During package installation on developer machines or CI/CD runners, Scarf transmits package name, host OS, Node.js version, and runner IP address to an external commercial service.
findings.impact: Build-host metadata and network origin disclosure; non-compliance with strict airgap/zero-trust data isolation requirements.
findings.remediation: Set ENV SCARF_ANALYTICS=false and DO_NOT_TRACK=1 in Dockerfile and CI environments, or use npm ci --ignore-scripts in production containers.
findings.regressionTest: Assert Dockerfile and CI workflow set SCARF_ANALYTICS=false.

findings.title: Unmaintained Upstream Dependency fluent-ffmpeg 2.1.3 Executing Subprocesses
findings.evidence: backend/package.json pins fluent-ffmpeg 2.1.3. Upstream project has been unmaintained for several years and relies on legacy async ^0.2.9.
findings.scenario: transcode.service.js and hls.service.js use fluent-ffmpeg to spawn FFmpeg processes. If input parameters or filter options contain unvalidated user input, process execution flaws or argument injection risks remain unpatched.
findings.impact: Unpatched subprocess execution risk and long-term maintenance liability.
findings.reproduction: Inspect backend/node_modules/fluent-ffmpeg/package.json dependencies and repository commit history.
findings.remediation: Replace fluent-ffmpeg with direct, modern child_process.execFile or execa calls using strict parameterized argument vectors.
findings.regressionTest: Add test case asserting video filenames with shell metacharacters and semicolons are rejected before FFmpeg spawn.

findings.title: Missing Standard Quality Gate Scripts (test, lint, typecheck) in package.json
findings.evidence: backend/package.json contains no 'test', 'lint', or 'typecheck' scripts. Only 'check' (node --check) and k6 scripts exist.
findings.scenario: Automated pipelines executing 'npm test' fail immediately with 'Missing script: test', preventing pre-merge automated testing.
findings.impact: Defects bypass standard CI/CD verification phases.
findings.reproduction: Execute 'npm test' in backend directory; returns exit code 1.
findings.remediation: Add standard 'test', 'lint', and 'check' scripts in backend/package.json.
findings.regressionTest: Execute 'npm test' and verify it runs automated unit/integration tests.

findings.title: Legacy Metadata and Single-Maintainer Risk for Streaming Multipart Parser (busboy 1.6.0)
findings.evidence: busboy@1.6.0 uses legacy non-SPDX 'licenses: [{ type: "MIT" }]' property, leaving 'license: undefined' in modern npm lockfiles.
findings.scenario: Enterprise automated compliance scanners flag busboy as missing license terms during compliance gates.
findings.impact: Compliance blocker during enterprise audits; bus factor risk on streaming multipart uploads.
findings.remediation: Configure license scanner override for busboy MIT license or monitor for modern SPDX-compliant releases.
findings.regressionTest: Run license verification asserting busboy resolves under MIT terms.

findings.title: Native Build Toolchain and Execution Surface (argon2 and msgpackr-extract)
findings.evidence: argon2 (0.45.1) and msgpackr-extract (3.0.4) specify hasInstallScript: true, running C++ build tools during installation.
findings.scenario: Arbitrary code execution during install if upstream tarballs are modified or hashes unverified. Requires temporary C++ compilers in Dockerfile.
findings.reproduction: Check hasInstallScript in package-lock.json for argon2 and msgpackr-extract.
findings.remediation: Ensure Dockerfile continues to isolate and purge virtual build tools, and enforce strict sha512 integrity verification.
findings.regressionTest: Verify production container image contains no gcc, g++, or make.
